C++ classes that declare methods in headers previously contributed no method symbols for those declarations. This extracts bodyless in-class methods, constructors, destructors, templates, operator overloads, and comma-separated declarations while keeping function-pointer data members classified as fields.

Calls through declarations now redirect to a unique out-of-line definition using AST names and lexical owners, including nested classes and inline namespaces. Ambiguous overloads remain conservative, and inherited calls retain their confidence and resolution metadata. Declaration signatures and type metadata preserve template constraints and shared specifiers.

Targets main directly. The former parent, PR #174 / trail 133 (C and C++ data members), has merged. Current main is integrated without conflicts while preserving the branch's existing commits and checkpoints.

Known limitation: C++ declaration IDs use signature hashes to survive overload insertion and reordering; signature edits change those IDs. This tradeoff is tracked in #214, and its associated trail finding was explicitly dismissed pending that design decision.

Validation of the integrated branch is in progress: full Go race suite, vet, build, formatting, and status-line tests. Hosted CI and fresh trail review will be checked before merge.
